::: {#thm-classes-partition}
#### Equivalence classes form a partition

Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on a set $S$ (@def-equivalence-relation).
Then the collection of the different equivalence classes $[a]$, for $a \in S$ (@def-equivalence-class),
is a partition of $S$ (@def-set-partition).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Each class $[a]$ is a subset of $S$, by @def-equivalence-class.
We check the three conditions of @def-set-partition.

**Nonempty.**
Since $\sim$ is reflexive, $a \sim a$, so $a \in [a]$.

**Different classes are disjoint.**
Let $[a]$ and $[b]$ be two classes that share an element $x$.
Then $x \sim a$ and $x \sim b$.
Since $\sim$ is symmetric, $a \sim x$,
and since $\sim$ is transitive, $a \sim b$.
So $[a] = [b]$, by @thm-related-classes.
So two different classes share no element.

**Every element is in a class.**
Each $a \in S$ is in its own class $[a]$, as in the first step.

:::

:::
